types.name: ClientMsg
types.doc: A message from a client to the server.

enum.name: Hello
enum.doc: Must be the first message on a connection.

named.name: schema_hash
named.doc: The client's `SCHEMA_HASH`; must equal the server's.

named.name: watch
named.doc:
Join watching: if another connection of the player drives its
body, it keeps driving and this one watches (`Control { driving:
false }` follows `Welcome`). A read-only client (a map, a query
bot), or a client reconnecting that was watching when it dropped,
sets it. With no driver, the connection drives either way.

named.name: bulk
named.doc:
How the client takes chunk data (new sections, their timelines,
unloads, and climate): `None` (simple bots), a WebSocket message
a frame; otherwise batched in `Bulk` messages, one per session
write, coded as it names or plainer (`BulkCodec`).

named.name: content
named.doc:
The stamp of the `Content` message the client holds (the stable
hash of its encoding, `forge_protocol::stamp::frame_stamp`),
after a reconnect: the server doesn't send it again when its own
is the same. `None`: send it.

named.name: opening
named.doc:
The client plays the opening (the web client, by default): its
player's first join takes the world's crash (the `crash` story
beat, waking at the wreck) if no player has yet; every other
first join gets the `flashback`. Bots and dev clients (the SDK
by default, smoke tests) leave it false, so they never take the
crash from the first person to play.

enum.name: Command
enum.doc: A command; answered by `CommandResult` with the same `seq`.

named.name: seq
named.doc: Chosen by the client to match the result.

enum.name: Subscribe
enum.doc:
Starts (or replaces) a live query. Its whole result follows
immediately as `Resync`, or, when resuming, a `Resync` or an
`Update` patching the value the client already has.

named.name: sub
named.doc: Chosen by the client to identify the subscription.

named.name: args
named.doc:
The query's arguments, encoded like a struct's fields (no bytes
for a query without arguments).

named.name: resume
named.doc: The result the client already has, after a reconnect.

enum.name: Unsubscribe
enum.doc: Stops a live query.

enum.name: Ping
enum.doc: Clock sync; answered by `Pong`.

named.name: client_time
named.doc: The client's clock, in milliseconds; echoed back.

enum.name: Chat
enum.doc: A chat line, broadcast to everyone. Not logged.

enum.name: SetInterest
enum.doc:
Sets the area whose chunks this connection receives: every section
within `radius_h` chunks of `center` horizontally (a square) and
`radius_v` vertically, nearest first, as `Section`s; then edits.
Sections leave with `SectionUnload` once more than two chunks beyond
the radius. Radii are capped by the server (16 and 8). For players
without dev rights the center is clamped to within the radii of the
player's body. An area reaching past the world's edge (block
coordinates outside `i32`) is refused with `InterestRejected`, and
the previous area stays. Several in one flush count as the last.
Not logged; changes nothing in the world. Without it, no chunks are
sent, and position queries answer as for hidden blocks.

named.name: center
named.doc: The chunk the area is centered on.

enum.name: Input
enum.doc:
One tick of movement input, sent 20 times a second while the
player's body is controlled. The server keeps a few per player
(dropping the oldest past 10, and any `seq` not above the last one
it took), applies at most one per movement tick, and acknowledges
it with `PlayerState`. Not logged; changes nothing but the body.

named.name: seq
named.doc: Increases by one per input; acknowledged by `PlayerState`.

named.name: input
named.doc: What the player wants to do this tick.

enum.name: TakeControl
enum.doc:
Takes control of the player's body from the player's other
connection (a "Play here" button): this connection drives it from
now on, and the one that drove watches. Answered by
`Control { driving: true }` (the other gets `driving: false`); start
sending `Input`s after it, numbered from the last `PlayerState`.

enum.name: Report
enum.doc:
A report for the world's operator: an error the client hit, a
problem the player describes, or a telemetry sample. The server
writes it to a file in the world's `reports` directory with the
world's version and time and both builds. Not logged, never sent to
other clients, and rate-limited per player alongside chat (dropped
past the limit). No reply.

named.name: text
named.doc: What happened, in the client's or the player's words.

named.name: stats
named.doc:
The client's numbers at the time, as JSON text (frame times,
device, position); written into the file as JSON when it parses.

named.name: build
named.doc:
The client's build: its git commit, `-dirty` if built from
changed files.

named.name: image
named.doc: A JPEG of the screen; empty for none.

enum.name: Holding
enum.doc:
After a reconnect, before `SetInterest`: what the client still holds
of the area it will ask for, by chunk column, so the server sends
only what changed while it was away (and nothing at all into an
unchanged world, across a server restart too). The server checks a
column when its stream first reaches it, building the column's
claimed sections as it would to send them: equal digests mark them
held without sending anything, a different section digest sends the
column again, a different timelines digest its `SectionTimelines`
only, a different piles digest its sections' `SectionPiles` only, a
different climate stamp its `ColumnClimate`. Columns outside
the area are ignored. Sent in parts when large; `last` on the last.
Accepted only before the connection's first `SetInterest`.

named.name: columns
named.doc: The columns held (each once over all parts).

enum.name: EntityResync
enum.doc:
The client's entities no longer follow the entity stream (a frame
didn't apply: `crate::entity::StreamError`): the server's next
`EntityStream` frame is a key frame, sent even if nothing changed,
holding everything in the watched area. The client ignores frames
until it arrives.

enum.name: Ack
enum.doc:
Chunk data taken: the bytes of every `Bulk` message the client has
taken so far on this connection (each counted whole, as its
WebSocket message's length: compressed, as it came, not inflated),
sent after each one it takes. The
first, `bytes: 0` right after `Hello`, turns on flow control: the
server keeps no more chunk data in flight than the link delivers in
a round trip and about 50 ms more, measured from these, so it never
queues in front of inputs' results, entity frames, or chat. A
client that never sends one gets chunk data as fast as the server
builds it. Only for clients that take chunk data batched
(`Hello.bulk`); handled by the connection itself, never by the
world, and not rate-limited.

named.name: bytes
named.doc: Bulk bytes taken since `Hello`, in all.

enum.name: Hold
enum.doc:
What the player holds now: the hotbar slot in hand. Sent when it
changes; the server shows it to others (the item in that slot, on
the player's entity: `crate::entity`'s held field). Not logged;
changes nothing in the world, and breaking takes its slot from
`Command::BreakWith`, not from this. Rate-limited with the other
small messages.

enum.name: Pose
enum.doc:
How the player's body looks to others: where it looks and the block
it is breaking (`crate::entity`'s look and work fields). Sent when
either changes enough to see (the web client: the look by 2/256 of
a turn or more, at most 5 times a second; the work when it starts,
stops, or moves to another block). Not logged; changes nothing in
the world, and breaking still takes `Command::Break`. The server
keeps a work target only within reach of the body, clamps the rest,
and adds the one-shot actions itself (a break, place, or use that
went through; hurt; knocked out). Rate-limited with the other small
messages; ignored from a connection that is only watching.

named.name: yaw
named.doc:
Facing, in 1/256 of a turn: 0 looks toward +z, 64 toward +x
(the camera's yaw).

named.name: pitch
named.doc:
Up or down, in 1/256 of a turn: -64 straight down, 0 level, 64
straight up (clamped to that).

named.name: work
named.doc: The block being broken, if any.

types.name: BulkCodec
types.doc:
How the frames in a `ServerMsg::Bulk` are coded. A client names the
most it accepts in `Hello.bulk`; each `Bulk` says what it used, so a
server may send any codec up to it (small batches go as they are).

enum.name: None
enum.doc: As they are: each frame its length (a varint) and its bytes.

enum.name: Deflate
enum.doc:
The same, then compressed with raw deflate (RFC 1951), which
browsers inflate natively (`DecompressionStream("deflate-raw")`).
Sent for a batch whose data is over 1 KiB and smaller compressed;
a client that names it still gets `None` for the rest.

types.name: Stamp
types.doc:
A 64-bit stamp, split in halves so a JavaScript number holds each:
forge-core's stable hash (`forge_protocol::stamp`). Never 0.

struct.name: hi
struct.doc: The high 32 bits.

struct.name: lo
struct.doc: The low 32 bits.

types.name: Command
types.doc: A player command.

enum.name: Place
enum.doc: Places the block of the item in `slot` at `pos`.

named.name: slot
named.doc: Inventory slot holding the item to place.

named.name: facing
named.doc: Which way the block faces; checked and normalized by its orient.

enum.name: Break
enum.doc: Breaks the block at `pos`.

named.name: eye
named.doc:
Where the breaker looks from, when that isn't its body's eye: a
dev flying its camera, whose body stays where flight began. A
felled tree falls away from it. Honored for dev connections
only; anyone else's break uses its body.

enum.name: Dev
enum.doc: A dev command; needs a `--dev` server and a `dev` token.

enum.name: Use
enum.doc:
Use the block at `pos` with the item in `slot` in hand: an elder
gives what is due, a keeper eats their dryad tree's ripe fruit, a
held can acts on water or a growth.

enum.name: StoragePut
enum.doc: Moves `count` whole items from `slot` into the storage at `pos`.

enum.name: StorageTake
enum.doc:
Moves `count` whole items of `item` from the storage at `pos` into
`slot` (empty, or holding the same item with room).

named.name: slot
named.doc: Inventory slot to put them in.

enum.name: InventoryMove
enum.doc:
Moves `count` whole items from inventory slot `from` to slot `to`:
into an empty slot, onto the same item with room, or, when `to`
holds something else and `count` is all of `from`, swapping the
two stacks.

named.name: to
named.doc: The slot to put them in.

enum.name: TakePile
enum.doc:
Takes the piles lying in the cell `cell` (a tap on a heap) into the
inventory, as many of each as fit; checked for reach like a break.
Refused if nothing lies there or nothing fits.

enum.name: Drop
enum.doc:
Drops `count` whole items from `slot` onto the ground as a pile in
`cell` (the client picks a cell a little ahead of the player, out of
pickup reach); checked for reach like a break. The pile settles like
any other: down to a firm cell, merged with a pile nearby.

enum.name: Recall
enum.doc:
Starts a recall: the body goes home once it has held still for
[`RECALL_MS`] (see `Recall`). Moving, jumping, a break, place, use,
drop, or pile tap, being hurt, or a knockout breaks it. Refused
while one runs, or with the body already home.

enum.name: StopRecall
enum.doc: Stops the recall in progress, if any (`Recall { Broken: Stopped }`).

enum.name: Make
enum.doc:
Makes `count` of a make recipe (one of `ServerMsg::Recipes`) by
hand, after the player held it for `count` times the recipe's
steps: the server holds each player to a budget of making time like
its mining credit, and refuses a make that comes too soon ("making
too fast"). Its inputs come from the inventory, the pack before the
hotbar; its outputs go where pickups go. Refused, naming what is
missing, if an input is short or the outputs don't fit.

named.name: count
named.doc: How many times over, at least 1.

named.name: at
named.doc:
The station's cell (`MakeInfo.at`), checked for reach like a
break; `None` for a recipe made anywhere.

enum.name: BreakWith
enum.doc:
Breaks the block at `pos` with the item in inventory `slot` in
hand: a tool breaks the materials it lists faster, and blocks of
its tier (ore needs a pick); anything else breaks as `Break` does,
by hand. Refused, naming the least tool that would do, if the block
needs a better one. The server paces breaks by the time with what
is in that slot ([`ContentView::hand`], [`ItemInfo::tool`]).

enum.name: Attack
enum.doc:
Strikes the wild creature `entity` (its id in the entity stream)
with what is in hotbar `slot` (an empty slot is a bare hand): its
`hit` against the creature's `tough` and `health`
(`ContentInfo.creatures`), three times over on one that hasn't
noticed the hunter. A blow alarms her herd; a kill drops her drops
as piles where she fell. Checked for reach from the body (about 4
blocks), and paced: at most one blow per [`ATTACK_MS`]. Answered
with a `ServerMsg::Hunt`.

enum.name: Feed
enum.doc:
Feeds the wild creature `entity` one of what is in hotbar `slot`:
it must be a food her species is tamed with, the body crouched
(the last input's `sneak`), she calm and within reach, and paced
with the blows: at most one `Attack` or `Feed` per [`ATTACK_MS`].
Each feed is trust; one of them tames her (`ServerMsg::Hunt`).

enum.name: Eat
enum.doc:
Eats one of the food in `slot` (`ItemInfo::food`): its `heal` back
at once, its `mend` over the next while. At most one per
[`ATTACK_MS`].

enum.name: Home
enum.doc:
Uses the creature home block at `pos` (a hay rack, hutch, or den:
`CreatureKeep::homes`): the player's kept creatures following it
within 16 blocks of it that it homes are homed there, as many as
it has room for (`CreatureKeep::capacity`). The first homing makes
the home the player's, with its fit. Checked for reach like a
break. Answered with a `ServerMsg::Home` (`HomeEvent::Homed`); a
follower led to her owner's home is homed there too, without one.

enum.name: Provision
enum.doc:
Feeds the creature home at `pos` `count` of the food in `slot`
(one its species eats: `CreatureKeep::feed`). Anyone may. Checked
for reach like a break. Answered with `HomeEvent::Provisioned`.

named.name: slot
named.doc: The slot the food comes from.

enum.name: Collect
enum.doc:
Takes what the creature home at `pos` has made (its owner's only)
into the inventory, as many as fit. Checked for reach like a break.
Answered with `HomeEvent::Collected`.

enum.name: BreakThrough
enum.doc:
`BreakWith` for a tool that breaks through (`ToolInfo::depth` 2:
the mattock): breaks the block at `pos`, then the one behind it,
away from `face` (the face struck, turned toward the breaker), if
that one would break too (not air, not beyond the tool, nothing in
it). The server paces the pair by both blocks' times with what is
in `slot`, as clients time it, and logs two breaks. The block
behind may be a block past reach. Refused if `face` isn't turned
toward the breaker's eye. With any other tool, `BreakWith`.

enum.name: Trust
enum.doc:
Trusts the player called `name` in the sender's land (its tree's
reach), or, with `on` false, stops: inside a tree's reach only its
owner and those it trusts build, break, use its storages and work
its machines. Refused for the sender's own name, a name no player
has, a change that changes nothing, or a list already full (64).
Trust is the player's, kept before it plants and wherever its tree
stands. The tree's `TreeView::trusted` lists it.

named.name: name
named.doc: The player's name, as it joined.

enum.name: Swing
enum.doc:
Swings what is in hotbar `slot` (an empty slot is a bare hand; its
`hit` is the damage): at husk `target` (an entity id from
[`HUSK_ENTITY_BASE`] up), or, with none, at the nearest husk the
swing reaches. Judged where the husks were at world step `seen`
(the low 32 bits of the step the client drew them at), rewound at
most 6 steps (300 ms) from the last completed step and never
ahead of it: within 4 blocks across and 3 up or down of the body,
in the half in front of it (the last `Pose` yaw). A blow in a
husk's wind-up staggers it. A creature `target` is an `Attack`.
Paced with `Attack` and `Feed` ([`ATTACK_MS`]). Answered with
`ServerMsg::Fight` (`FightEvent::Hit`) before its `CommandResult`;
a swing that hits nothing is rejected with why.

named.name: target
named.doc: The husk, if one is aimed at (the soft lock's).

named.name: seen
named.doc: The step the client drew the husks at, low 32 bits.

enum.name: Charm
enum.doc:
Casts the charm in inventory `slot` (an item with
`ItemInfo::charm`) facing `aim` (1/256 turn, as `Pose`'s yaw): at
husk `target` (the soft lock's) or, with none, the nearest its
shape reaches, judged where the husks were at world step `seen` as
a swing is. Spends the charm's `charge` of the item (logged).
Refused with why, spending nothing: too few held, cooling down (its
`cooldown_ms`, per player and item; dev players aren't paced), not
in a fight (within 32 blocks of a husk), or a shaped effect that
reaches no husk. Answered with `ServerMsg::Fight`
(`FightEvent::Cast`, then a `Hit` for each husk it hit) before its
`CommandResult`; a heal sends `Vitals`, a dash a `PlayerState`.

named.name: slot
named.doc: The inventory slot the charm is in.

named.name: target
named.doc: The husk, if one is aimed at (the soft lock's).

named.name: seen
named.doc: The step the client drew the husks at, low 32 bits.

enum.name: Companion
enum.doc:
Calls the companion at husk `target` (or the husk winding up
nearest it): it harries, staggering a wind-up (FR4). In a Spire
run, the shrine's stand-in fox; refused elsewhere ("no companion
with you"), while it is winded, and for 12 s after a harry.

named.name: target
named.doc: The husk, if one is aimed at (the soft lock's).

enum.name: Gather
enum.doc:
The shrine's root door (FR4): opens a gathering in the ring by the
shrine if none is open (the body within 8 blocks of the ring),
joins the open one (the body in the ring: 8 blocks across), or,
with `now` from a player who has joined, takes the party down at
once. A gathering is open 15 s, or until four have joined; then
the ones still in the ring go down together (`RunEvent::Descend`).

named.name: now
named.doc: Go down now, without waiting out the 15 s.

named.name: floor
named.doc:
The floor to go down to (SP2; 0 is FR4's root hall). The one
who opens the gathering picks it; joiners go where it goes.

named.name: seals
named.doc:
The seals the one who opens the gathering sets beside its key
(P5.5, `Floors.seals`): at most three, each a different card;
spent as the party goes down, given back by a restart. Only the
gathering's opener sets them; a joiner's are ignored.

enum.name: SetRune
enum.doc:
Sets the word item in `word_slot` (carved, or out of a relic) into
the tool in `slot` (one
tool, not a stack) at the runeforge whose forge stone is at `at`
(RW3): the word must be the tool's own rune (a copper pick takes
*heat*). The word is used up; the tool keeps its rune, charge 0.
The forge's frame must stand and be the player's to use.

enum.name: Charge
enum.doc:
Puts the rune tool in `slot` into the charge slot of the runeforge
whose forge stone is at `at`, where it fills from the forge's pool
of its rune's element (a mana a second, a charge a mana); or, if a
tool of the player's charges there, takes it back into `slot` (an
empty slot), its charge floored to whole units (RW3).

named.name: slot
named.doc: The slot the tool comes from or goes to.

enum.name: CopyFrame
enum.doc:
Copies the whole frame standing over `at` (any of its cells: a
player's frame or a standing stone's ancient one) onto the scroll
in `slot` (RW6): a blank becomes a rune scroll holding the frame,
a rune scroll is written over. The world logs the copy as the text
it read (`WriteScroll`). Within reach of `at`.

enum.name: WriteScroll
enum.doc:
Writes `text` (a scroll line, `fw1:ward3/fire.burn.ring`, at most
160 characters; docs/engine/runes-scrolls.md) onto the scroll in
`slot` (RW6): pasting a frame. A blank becomes a rune scroll, a
rune scroll is written over; text that doesn't read is refused
with why.

enum.name: Party
enum.doc:
Takes the player's kin (herd, member: a card of the `kin` query)
as a companion (`join`), or sends her home (KN3). Joining, she
leaves her hearth's home and follows, on the surface and into the
Spire; at most three follow at once, and one resting (knocked out)
can't until her rest is over. Leaving, she goes back to the home
she left if it has room, else stays where she is. Refused with why.

named.name: join
named.doc: True to take her along, false to send her home.

enum.name: BreakRelic
enum.doc:
Breaks the Spire relic in `slot` (a card of the `relics` query) at
the runeforge whose forge stone is at `at` (SP4): the relic is
spent, and each word it held comes out as its word's item, to set
into a tool or a charm (`Command::SetRune`). Not inside the Spire;
refused with why when the words have no room.

enum.name: AltarFloor
enum.doc:
Sets the floor the player's altar forges keys for (P5.1; the
`altar` query shows it): floor 1 always, a deeper one once the
player holds the camp above it. Its list is drawn when first
chosen and kept until a key forges or it is rerolled. Refused with
why (no altar, the floor shut).

enum.name: AltarReroll
enum.doc:
Draws the player's altar's list again for its floor (P5.1): the
first reroll of a list is free, each later one takes as many root
shards as rerolls before it. Refused with why (no altar, too few
shards).

enum.name: Pin
enum.doc:
Pins a make recipe at the top of the player's tome (phase 8, K2),
or clears the hand pin (`None`), which leaves the path's default:
the recipe the last milestone reached pins. Refused for a recipe
the player doesn't know. Kept by the server beside the world for
every device of the player (not logged, not world state); sent back
in `ServerMsg::Knowledge.pin`.

named.name: recipe
named.doc: The make recipe (`MakeInfo.recipe`), or none to clear.

enum.name: Seen
enum.doc:
Marks make recipes seen in the player's tome (K2): they are no
longer new in `ServerMsg::Knowledge.unseen`. A recipe the player
doesn't know yet is skipped (it is new once learned). Kept like
`Pin`; at most [`MAX_SEEN`] a command.

types.name: BlockPos
types.doc: A block position in world coordinates.

struct.name: x
struct.doc: East-west.

struct.name: y
struct.doc: Up-down.

struct.name: z
struct.doc: North-south.

types.name: Facing
types.doc:
Which way a block faces. North is −z, south +z, west −x, east +x.
A block's orient decides which facings it accepts; blocks without one
face north.

types.name: EntityPos
types.doc:
An entity position: chunk index plus offset within the chunk in 1/4096
block per axis.

struct.name: cx
struct.doc: Chunk x.

struct.name: cy
struct.doc: Chunk y.

struct.name: cz
struct.doc: Chunk z.

struct.name: ox
struct.doc: Offset x within the chunk, in 1/4096 block.

struct.name: oy
struct.doc: Offset y within the chunk, in 1/4096 block.

struct.name: oz
struct.doc: Offset z within the chunk, in 1/4096 block.

types.name: DevCommand
types.doc: Commands for setting up tests and controlling time.

enum.name: Give
enum.doc: Sets an inventory slot's contents (`count` 0 empties it).

enum.name: SetBlock
enum.doc: Sets a block directly, skipping placement rules.

named.name: facing
named.doc: Which way it faces; checked and normalized by its orient.

enum.name: Teleport
enum.doc: Moves the player's body.

enum.name: Pause
enum.doc: Stops world time.

enum.name: Resume
enum.doc: Restarts world time.

enum.name: Step
enum.doc: Advances world time by `steps`.

enum.name: AdvanceTo
enum.doc: Advances world time to `time`.

enum.name: Present
enum.doc:
Marks this player present or not: a present player's body watches
the chunks around it, where the world runs live physics (see the
engine's live module). Connecting makes a player present; this
overrides that while it stays connected (a builder bot that
shouldn't watch), and its last connection closing makes it absent.

enum.name: GrowTree
enum.doc:
Grows a tree of a built-in shape (`oak`, `large_oak`), or of a
species of `forge:standard` v2's default settings (`birch`,
`spruce`, `willow`, ...: `features.species` in the content), with its
trunk's lowest layer at `pos` (that layer's corner with the smallest
x and z): its natural wood replaces what is there, its leaves fill
only air. The same shape and seed at the same place give the same
tree. Logged as the blocks it sets, together.

enum.name: SpawnHusk
enum.doc:
Stands a training-dummy husk up at `pos`, facing `yaw` (1/256 of a
turn): a dev target for fights (FR1). It stays where it stands,
winds up at the nearest body within 6 blocks every 1.5 s, strikes,
and stands up whole 3 s after it goes down. At most 24.

enum.name: ClearHusks
enum.doc: Every husk goes.

enum.name: SpawnHuskOf
enum.doc:
Stands a husk of `species` (an index into `ContentInfo.creatures`,
a husk-tier one) up at `pos`, facing `yaw` (FR2): it wakes, hunts
the nearest body, strikes, and is gone 2 s after it goes down. Husks
never spawn on their own; this and the tests are the only way in.
At most 24 (with the dummies).

enum.name: Teach
enum.doc:
The player knows these fruit of the dryad too, as if it had eaten
them (RW7): knowledge bits (`ServerMsg::Knowledge.fruit`), each a
fruit of the content's dryad. Logged; its connections are sent the
`Knowledge` and each newly known fruit's vision, as for eating one.

enum.name: Forget
enum.doc:
The player no longer knows these fruit (PG1): knowledge bits, each
a fruit of the content's dryad, as `Teach`'s. What it made stays.
Logged; its connections are sent the `Knowledge`.

enum.name: SetBar
enum.doc:
The bar of `element` (0 fire, 1 water, 2 wind, 3 earth) of the
tree whose heart is at `heart` (any player's) holds `mana` now, at
most full (PG1): past a notch its fruit ripens, four full bars stage
the tree up, and its heart eats on from there. Logged.

enum.name: SetPool
enum.doc:
The pool at `pos` holds `mana` of its element now, at most its
capacity (PG1): fills or drains it. Logged.

enum.name: SetHealth
enum.doc:
The player's health, 1 to its most (PG1): a dev set never knocks
out. Live, like all vitals; its connections are sent the `Vitals`.

enum.name: GiveRune
enum.doc:
Puts a charm or rune tool in a slot (PG1): `item` a rune item (a
charm, a rune pick), `words` its words (`ContentInfo.words`
indices, an action it takes first, at most three), charged
`charge` (at most its cap). Never over a rune tool. Logged.

enum.name: SetBond
enum.doc:
The player's kin (herd, member: as the `kin` query's cards) has a
bond of `permille` thousandths of full now (KN3): at 1000 her
second word and her look are hers. Logged.

enum.name: KnockOut
enum.doc:
Knocks the player out at once, as if `cause` took its last health
(FX1: journeys knock out in one step): its knockout is a real one,
logged (`Downed`) and told as any is, a satchel and the wake
included. Refused while live play can't log it.

named.name: cause
named.doc: What knocked it out (a drowning wakes on its last firm ground).

enum.name: SetCamps
enum.doc:
Sets the player's Spire camps outright (SP5): bit `n - 1` for floor
`n`'s, as passing its test gives it. Logged.

enum.name: SetSpring
enum.doc:
The wellspring of the floor run the player is in holds `mana` now,
at most full (FX3a: a riddle try on an empty spring, in one step).
Live, like the run's test; its run is sent the `Trial`.

enum.name: FellGuardian
enum.doc:
The guardian of the floor run the player is in falls at once, as
if struck to nothing (RL3: a dev's setup for a kill a test doesn't
fight): her fall is a real one, logged (`GuardianFelled`, the
world's first if none fell yet), her room cleared and her camp's
relics banked as after any fall. Refused unless she stands
unwarded (her coil or her drowning). Live, like the run's fight.

enum.name: DirectFight
enum.doc:
A director's input into the fight the player is in (P6.2b: so a
client's zones, marks and broken wind-ups can be seen before a
director sends them). It goes in through `World::direct`, journaled
and told as a director's. Dev only, as every dev command.

enum.name: Reach
enum.doc:
The player reaches a milestone of the path (phase 8: `Event::Reach`,
a tester's way to set any progress in one step): it knows what the
milestone teaches from now on. Refused for a name the path lacks or
a milestone reached already. Logged.

types.name: NameId
types.doc: A block or item name, as an index into `Welcome.names`.

types.name: HurtCause
types.doc: What hurt a player's body (`forge_core::vitals::Cause`).

enum.name: Fall
enum.doc: A fall of more than four blocks.

enum.name: Drown
enum.doc: Drowning: the eye in a fluid with no air left.

enum.name: Creature
enum.doc: A creature.

types.name: DevDirect
types.doc:
What a `DevCommand::DirectFight` puts into the player's fight (P6.2b):
a director's zone, order or fix. Lengths are in fight units (1/4096
block), times in steps (1/20 s).

enum.name: Zone
enum.doc:
A zone (`FightEvent::Zone`), anchored at the player's feet plus
(`dx`, `dz`).

named.name: id
named.doc: Its group: a shelter's lees share its id.

named.name: shape
named.doc: Its shape, drawn from its anchor along `aim`.

named.name: dx
named.doc: Its anchor's x from the player's feet, 1/4096 block.

named.name: dz
named.doc: Its anchor's z from the player's feet, 1/4096 block.

named.name: follow
named.doc: True to pin it to the player's body until it lands (`on`).

named.name: aim
named.doc: Its facing (an arc's or a line's), 1/256 of a turn.

named.name: reach
named.doc: An arc's or a ring's radius, a line's length, 1/4096 block.

named.name: wind
named.doc: Steps until it lands (1 at least).

named.name: damage
named.doc: What it does to a body (its rule shares or scales it).

enum.name: Order
enum.doc:
The fight's strongest standing husk (the most full health: a boss)
winds up its species' move `strike`, aimed at the player. Refused
if its species has no such move, or it is busy (winding up,
striking, staggered).

named.name: strike
named.doc:
The move, 1 up (an index into its creature's `fight.moves`
plus one; as `HuskView.strike`).

enum.name: Fix
enum.doc:
That same husk hunts the player for `steps` from now
(`FightEvent::Marked`); 0 clears its fix.

types.name: StrikeShape
types.doc: The ground a husk's strike covers.

enum.name: Arc
enum.doc:
A 90-degree sector in front of it, `reach` out, drawn from where it
stood as it wound up.

enum.name: Line
enum.doc: A strip along its aim, `reach` long and `width` either side.

enum.name: Ring
enum.doc: All round it, `reach` out (SP3: a slam, a drowning pull).

types.name: ZoneRule
types.doc: How a zone hurts (`FightEvent::Zone`, P6.1d).

enum.name: Burst
enum.doc: Each body inside takes its damage.

enum.name: Shelter
enum.doc:
Each body inside it and outside every live `Lee` of its id takes
its damage: get behind cover.

enum.name: Lee
enum.doc: Hurts no one: cover from the `Shelter`s of its id.

enum.name: Spread
enum.doc:
On a body: each other body inside takes its damage, and that body
too if any other is inside. Kept apart, it costs nothing.

enum.name: Stack
enum.doc:
Shared by the bodies inside: each takes its damage over them
(rounded up), as if `need` stood in it while fewer do; none
inside, and every body takes it whole.

enum.name: Soak
enum.doc:
Soaked: `need` or more inside each take a quarter of its damage;
fewer, and every body takes it whole.

types.name: Resume
types.doc:
The result a client holds for a query it resubscribes to after a
reconnect. If the server still knows that value, it answers with a
patch from it instead of the whole result.

struct.name: version
struct.doc: The world version of that result.

struct.name: hash
struct.doc: The stable hash of its encoding, 16 hex digits.

types.name: ChunkPos
types.doc:
A chunk's position, in chunks: the section holding blocks
`16x..16x+15` and so on.

struct.name: x
struct.doc: East-west.

struct.name: y
struct.doc: Up-down.

struct.name: z
struct.doc: North-south.

types.name: MoveInput
types.doc: One tick of player input (`forge_core::movement::MoveInput`).

struct.name: move_x
struct.doc:
Wished direction east-west in world space, -127 to 127 (127 is full
speed; values past the limit count as it).

struct.name: move_z
struct.doc: Wished direction north-south, -127 to 127.

struct.name: jump
struct.doc: Jump; in a fluid, swim up; on a ladder, climb.

struct.name: sneak
struct.doc: Sneak: slower, and holds position on a ladder.

struct.name: sprint
struct.doc: Sprint: faster on foot.

struct.name: glide
struct.doc:
Glide: in the air and falling, with a glider (`ItemInfo::glides`)
in hand; the server ignores it without one.

struct.name: dodge
struct.doc:
Dodge: a dash along the wished direction with i-frames, on foot
and not gliding, when the last dodge's cooldown is over
(`forge_core::movement::DODGE_TICKS`); with no direction, i-frames
in place.

types.name: ReportKind
types.doc: What a `Report` is.

enum.name: Error
enum.doc: An error the client hit, sent by itself.

enum.name: Player
enum.doc: A problem the player reported, in their words.

enum.name: Telemetry
enum.doc:
A periodic sample of how the client runs (frame times, GPU time,
what it holds), sent unless the player turned it off.

types.name: HeldColumn
types.doc: What a client holds of one chunk column (`ClientMsg::Holding`).

struct.name: x
struct.doc: The column's chunk x.

struct.name: z
struct.doc: The column's chunk z.

struct.name: y0
struct.doc:
The lowest section of the bitmap: bit `i` of `held` is section
`y0 + i`.

struct.name: held
struct.doc: The sections held, as a bitmap from `y0`.

struct.name: digest
struct.doc:
The digest of the held sections' stamps, in y order
(`forge_protocol::stamp::column_digest`).

struct.name: tl_digest
struct.doc:
The digest of the timelines stamps of those of them with timelines
(`None`: none has).

struct.name: climate
struct.doc: The stamp of the column's climate held (`None`: none).

struct.name: piles
struct.doc:
The digest of the piles stamps of those of the held sections with
piles (`forge_protocol::stamp::piles_stamp`; `None`: none has).

types.name: Working
types.doc:
The block a player is breaking, as others are shown it
(`ClientMsg::Pose`, the entity stream's work field): what to crack and
how far, and how long the whole break takes, so a watcher runs the
cracks on by itself until the next change.

struct.name: pos
struct.doc: The block.

struct.name: progress
struct.doc: How far along the break is, in 64ths (0 to 64).

struct.name: steps
struct.doc: How long the whole break takes, in 50 ms steps (1 to 1200).

types.name: ServerMsg
types.doc: A message from the server to a client.

enum.name: Welcome
enum.doc: Reply to an accepted `Hello`.

named.name: names
named.doc: The name table: `names[i]` is the name of `NameId(i)`.

named.name: dev
named.doc: Whether this connection may use dev commands.

named.name: build
named.doc:
The server's build: its git commit, `-dirty` if built from
changed files (`unknown` when not built from a checkout).

named.name: observer
named.doc:
The connection only observes (an `observer` token, such as a
Discord bot's): no player joined and no body; `player` is 0 and
`player_name` the token's name. It gets broadcasts and global
queries; its commands are refused and its moves ignored.

named.name: spire
named.doc:
The Spire on the surface (SP1), in a world with one: where its
foot stands, how tall it is, and the blight about it. Its news
(the week, the first fall) follows as `ServerMsg::Spire`.

named.name: sea_level
named.doc:
The world's sea level, from its generator: `forge:standard`'s
settings' `sea_level` (the sea's top water block's y),
`forge:flat`'s ground. Null for a generator without one.
Clients draw the sea's fog and mist from it.

enum.name: Rejected
enum.doc: Reply to a bad `Hello`; the server then closes the connection.

enum.name: CommandResult
enum.doc: The outcome of a `Command`.

enum.name: Update
enum.doc:
A change to a subscription's result: apply `patch` to the last
result the client has (from `Resync` or earlier updates).

named.name: version
named.doc: The world version the new result reflects.

named.name: hash
named.doc:
The stable hash of the new result's encoding, 16 hex digits; a
client whose patched result hashes differently resubscribes.

named.name: patch
named.doc: What changed. Empty when a resumed result is already current.

enum.name: Resync
enum.doc:
A subscription's whole result: the first one, and whenever a patch
isn't possible or isn't smaller.

named.name: version
named.doc: The world version the result reflects.

enum.name: QueryFailed
enum.doc: A query could not run.

enum.name: Clock
enum.doc:
The world clock; sent on pause, resume, step, advance, and every 5 s
while running.

enum.name: Pong
enum.doc: Reply to `Ping`.

enum.name: Chat
enum.doc: A chat line.

enum.name: Section
enum.doc:
One whole section in the connection's interest area, replacing any
the client holds at `pos` (and its timelines: they follow as
`SectionTimelines` when it has any). Hidden blocks are sent as
`forge:stone`.

enum.name: SectionEdit
enum.doc:
Blocks that changed in a section the client holds, including every
block whose visibility changed (an exposed block's real identity).
A command's edits reach its sender before its `CommandResult`.

named.name: stamp
named.doc:
The stamp of the section's encoding after the edit, as a whole
`Section` of it would have (`forge_protocol::stamp`): what the
client holds now, for its `Holding` after a reconnect.

enum.name: SectionUnload
enum.doc:
Sections that left the interest area; the client may drop them.
Sent in the chunk data lane, behind any `Section` for the same
positions, at most `MAX_UNLOAD_BATCH` (512) positions per message.

enum.name: SectionTimelines
enum.doc:
The timelines of a section's growing and timed blocks (saplings,
compiled tree spots), replacing any sent before: the client draws
them by its clock with no per-stage traffic. Sent after a `Section`
that has any, and again when they change (empty when none are left).

named.name: entries
named.doc: Each timed block's steps, by index.

enum.name: InterestRejected
enum.doc:
A `SetInterest` was refused (its area reaches past the world's
edge); the previous interest area stays.

enum.name: EntityFrame
enum.doc:
No longer sent: entities travel in `EntityStream`. Kept so the
messages after it keep their numbers. Was: live entities in the
client's watched area that changed since the last frame, whole.

named.name: entities
named.doc:
Entities that appeared in the area or changed (moved, slowed,
fuse ticked), whole, in id order.

named.name: removed
named.doc: Ids of entities that went away or left the area, in order.

enum.name: Movement
enum.doc:
The content's movement rules, sent right after `Welcome`: clients
predict their body with these and never ship their own copy.

named.name: materials
named.doc:
Each block's movement material, by `NameId` (names that aren't
blocks get air's).

enum.name: PlayerState
enum.doc:
The player's body as the server stepped it: after every movement
tick that applied one of its inputs, and when the server moved it
itself (on connect, after a teleport). Priority lane. A predicting
client resets to `state` and replays its inputs after `seq`.

named.name: seq
named.doc: The last input applied (0 before any).

named.name: state
named.doc: The body's movement state after it.

named.name: tick_us
named.doc:
How long the server's last movement tick took, in microseconds
(diagnostics).

enum.name: Content
enum.doc:
The content clients need, sent right after `Welcome` (before
`Movement`): every block's and item's data (how it looks, how it
places, what a right click does), the recipes, and the packs they
came from. Clients build their tables from it and ship no copy of
their own. It is always whole, never a patch, so a server can send
it again mid-session when its content changes; a client then
replaces everything it built from the last one, names included.

enum.name: ColumnClimate
enum.doc:
The climate of one chunk column's 16 x 16 block columns at their
surface (`forge_core::generator::ColumnClimate`): what clients tint
grass, leaves, and water by, and show in a debug view. Sent in the
chunk data lane once per connection, right before the first
`Section` of the column, and forgotten (on both sides) when the
column's last section is unloaded; sent again if the column comes
back. Never sent for generators without a climate (`forge:flat`
without one, `forge:standard` v1). Climate is a pure function of the
world's seed and settings, so it never changes while a column is
held.

named.name: temperature
named.doc:
Mean surface temperature per block column, in degrees Celsius
as a two's complement byte, index `x | z << 4`: 256 bytes, or 129
when sent as differences (`forge_protocol::climate`).

named.name: moisture
named.doc:
Moisture per block column, 0 (desert) to 100 (saturated), index
`x | z << 4`, encoded like `temperature`.

named.name: wind_x
named.doc:
The prevailing wind over the column, the way it blows: x and z
of a unit vector times 127, plus 128 (`forge_core::Generator::wind_at`;
a continent tile's in `forge:standard` v2, which leans its exposed
trees). Both 128 (no wind) where the generator has none.

named.name: tint
named.doc:
The drift of the land's greens at the column's four corners
(`forge_core::Generator::tint_at`; a `forge:standard` v2
geology's): a byte each, block corner `(x0, z0)` in the low
byte, then `(x0 + 16, z0)`, `(x0, z0 + 16)`, `(x0 + 16, z0 + 16)`,
where `(x0, z0)` is the column's first block. A byte's low
nibble is the hue (-7 cooler to 7 warmer), its high nibble the
saturation (-7 greyer to 7 richer), each a four-bit two's
complement; clients blend between the corners. 0 (no drift)
where the generator has none. Like the wind, not in the
climate's stamp: both are pure functions of the seed and settings.

enum.name: TreeFall
enum.doc:
A tree (or a cut branch) started to fall: sent once, when it is
felled, to every client whose interest area or watched chunks hold
the cut. Its blocks are already gone from the world (their section
edits follow in the chunk lane, or came first); a client draws them
as one rigid piece that creaks from `start`, turns about the hinge
toward `toward` from `tip` until `turned`, drops `drop` blocks until
`impact`, and lies there until `settle`, when its drops appear as
item entities. The server worked all of it out; clients only draw
it. A client that connects later never hears of it.

named.name: cut
named.doc: The block whose cut felled it.

named.name: blocks
named.doc: The blocks that fell, as they stood.

named.name: hinge_x
named.doc:
The hinge it turns about, from the cut block's lowest corner, in
1/4096 block: x.

named.name: toward
named.doc:
Which way it falls: one of 16 compass directions, 0 north (−z),
4 east (+x), 8 south, 12 west.

named.name: angle
named.doc: How far it turns, in degrees (90 lies flat).

named.name: drop
named.doc: Blocks it drops straight down after turning.

named.name: start
named.doc: World time it starts to creak.

named.name: tip
named.doc: When it starts to turn (6° tipped), after the creak.

named.name: turned
named.doc: When it stops turning (and starts to drop, if it does).

named.name: settle
named.doc: When its drops appear and it is gone.

enum.name: Control
enum.doc:
Whether this connection drives its player's body. One connection of
a player drives it, the newest; the player's other connections (a
second tab, an older device) watch: their `Input`s are dropped
without touching the body, their play commands are refused, and they
still get every `PlayerState` (the body as the driver moves it).
Sent when control moves to or from this connection: a newer
connection of the same player joined, one of them sent
`TakeControl`, or the driving one closed and this one, the newest
left, drives again. A connection that hasn't been told drives.

named.name: driving
named.doc:
True: this connection's inputs move the body (from the last
`PlayerState` on); false: it watches.

enum.name: Closed
enum.doc:
The server is about to close this connection, and why. The last
message on it; a client reconnects after `Stopping`, never after
`Kicked` or `Banned`.

enum.name: Sky
enum.doc:
The world's day (`forge_core::sky`): how long it is, where world
time 0 falls in it, and the moon's cycle. Sent right after
`Welcome`, and again after `Content` when the content changes. A
client works out the time of day, the sun, and the moon from these
and its synced clock, with no more traffic. No rule reads them.

named.name: day_steps
named.doc:
Steps in a day, sunrise to sunrise (28,800: 24 minutes). Sunset
is 68% of the way through.

named.name: start
named.doc: Where world time 0 falls in the day, in steps after sunrise.

named.name: moon_days
named.doc: Days in the moon's cycle, new to new.

named.name: first_day_extra
named.doc:
Steps the world's first day's light is drawn out by (FD1): until
the first sunset the sky runs slower, taking this many more
steps, then runs with world time, this far behind. 0 in worlds
made before FD1.

enum.name: Bulk
enum.doc:
Chunk data batched: the bulk-lane messages one session write takes
(`Section`, `SectionTimelines`, `SectionUnload`, `ColumnClimate`),
each a whole encoded `ServerMsg` with its length (a varint) before
it, in the order they would have come one by one. Sent only to
clients that asked in `Hello.bulk`, at most one a write, after the
write's other messages (a few dozen for a full 16-chunk view instead
of about 19,000 WebSocket messages). `forge_protocol::bulk` packs and
reads them.

enum.name: SectionPiles
enum.doc:
Every pile lying in one section (items at rest on the ground: see
`forge_sim`'s `pile` module), replacing what the client held of it.
Sent in the chunk lane right behind a `Section` that has any (a whole
`Section` clears a section's piles), and again, whole, when the
client's piles of a held section aren't known; otherwise changes come
as `SectionPilesDelta`. Empty when the last pile went.

named.name: piles
named.doc: Its piles, by index, item, and owner.

enum.name: SectionPilesDelta
enum.doc:
What changed in a held section's piles since the last `SectionPiles`
or delta the client got for it: piles added or changed, whole, and
piles gone. Built once a flush for every holder.

named.name: set
named.doc: Piles new or changed (their count), whole.

enum.name: Weather
enum.doc:
Storm fronts near this connection (`forge_core::weather`): the ones
it doesn't hold yet, and the ids of ones it may drop. A front is a
motion timeline, so a client works out rain, snow, gusts, and
thunder at any column and time from the fronts it holds, its
columns' climate, and `rules`, with no more traffic. A connection
holds the fronts that come within 2,048 blocks of its interest area
and live within ten minutes of now, plus the next slot's (sent
ahead), at most 48. Priority lane, at most one a second, only when
something changed. Never sent for worlds without weather. No rule
reads it yet.

named.name: rules
named.doc:
How fronts become rain, snow, and dust: sent with a
connection's first `Weather`, and again after `Content`. A
`Weather` that carries them holds the whole set: the client
replaces what it held.

named.name: fronts
named.doc: Fronts to hold, by id (an id already held is never sent again).

named.name: gone
named.doc: Ids of fronts to drop: ended, or gone out of reach.

enum.name: Vitals
enum.doc:
This connection's player's health and air (`forge_core::vitals`),
live state the server keeps for its body: never logged, full on
joining. Sent when either changes as a client shows it (health by
any amount, air by a bubble: [`AIR_PER_BUBBLE`] ticks) or the body
is hurt, and on connecting when not full or breathing by a word.
Never sent while both are full and unchanged and no word is on its
breath; a client assumes full, at breath 1, until told.

named.name: max_health
named.doc: Full health (20: ten leaves of two).

named.name: air
named.doc: Air, in movement ticks (1/20 s), 0 to `max_air`.

named.name: hurt
named.doc: What hurt the body since the last `Vitals`, if anything did.

named.name: breath
named.doc:
How many times as long its air lasts under water (FX3: a
Drowned kin's Deep Breath, its owner's or a nearby player's);
1 for none. Over 1, it also swims a third faster (its
`Movement` says so) and sees clearly under water. A change of
it alone sends a `Vitals`.

enum.name: Downed
enum.doc:
This connection's player was knocked out (its health reached zero)
and woke at home, logged as `Outcome::Downed`: every stack outside
its hotbar went into its satchel (owned piles, see `SectionPiles`)
from `at`, and its body now stands at `wake`. Sent before the
`PlayerState` that puts the body at `wake`; the waiting inputs the
server held for the body were dropped, so that state is a reset,
not a correction, and the next input is applied from there.

named.name: at
named.doc:
The cell its satchel was put from (it rests from there as any
dropped item does).

named.name: wake
named.doc:
Where its body woke: home (its dryad tree once planted, else
the crash site).

named.name: tree
named.doc:
It woke by its own dryad tree (true) or at the crash site, by
the wreck (false): what the knockout card says.

enum.name: EntityStream
enum.doc:
Live entities in the client's watched area that changed since its
last frame: the per-step traffic. A frame of the entity stream
(`crate::entity`: compact differences, each body stamped with its
movement step), on the priority lane after a batch of changes (at
most one a movement tick or world step) to each client whose
watched chunks hold something that changed, never when nothing did
(but for a key frame). A client that applies every frame in order
holds exactly the entities in its watched area; its first frame is
a key frame.

enum.name: Recall
enum.doc:
This connection's player's recall (`Command::Recall`), as the
server runs it: it began, it broke, or the body arrived home. Sent
to every connection of the player.

enum.name: Recipes
enum.doc:
What this connection's player can make by hand (`Command::Make`):
every make recipe, whatever it carries (a client works out which it
has the inputs for). Sent once at connect, right after `Content`'s
place, and again when the content changes.

enum.name: Trees
enum.doc:
The dryad trees this connection's player knows of: those whose
heart is within its interest area (at most [`TREES_SHOWN`], nearest
its body first), and its own always (for the compass), wherever it
stands. The whole set, sent when it changes: on connecting (if
there is any tree to show), when a tree in it changes or one comes
into or leaves it (planting, moving the interest area), and empty
when the last one leaves it.

named.name: trees
named.doc: The trees, its own first, then nearest first.

enum.name: Story
enum.doc:
A beat of the opening's story (`ContentView::story[beat]`): a card
of lines the client shows one at a time. Sent to every connection
of the player it happened to: `crash` on the first player's first
join, `flashback` on every later player's first join, `gift` when an
elder gives it the seed, `elder_carrying` or `elder_tree` when an
elder is used again, `planted` when its seed is planted.

named.name: at
named.doc:
Where it points: the nearest elder tree (the trunk's middle over
the ground) for `crash` and `flashback`, the elder used for its
beats, the heart for `planted`; none if there is nothing to
point to (no elder in the world).

enum.name: Hunt
enum.doc:
What this connection's player's `Command::Attack` or
`Command::Feed` did: sent to every connection of the player, just
before the command's `CommandResult`.

enum.name: Home
enum.doc:
What this connection's player's `Command::Home`, `Provision`, or
`Collect` did: sent to every connection of the player, just before
the command's `CommandResult`.

enum.name: Knowledge
enum.doc:
What this connection's player knows, and its tome's pin and marks
(phase 8, K2): sent whole after `Recipes` when it connects, again
after the content is reloaded, and to every connection of the
player whenever any of it changes: a fruit eaten (just before that
`Use`'s `CommandResult`), a recipe learned, a milestone reached, a
`Pin` or a `Seen`. A make recipe with a `MakeInfo.teaser` is made
only by a player whose `recipes` list it; any other only once
`known` has it.

named.name: fruit
named.doc:
The fruit it has eaten, by knowledge bit: `12 × stage + 3 ×
branch + notch` (branches fire, water, wind, earth; notches
Draw, Work, Wield), ascending.

named.name: recipes
named.doc:
The make recipes a fruit taught it, by id
(`MakeInfo.recipe`), in the `Recipes` order.

named.name: known
named.doc:
Every make recipe it knows (from the start, learned by holding,
taught by a milestone or a fruit), a bit each in the `Recipes`
order: recipe `i` is bit `i % 8` of byte `i / 8`. Trailing zero
bytes are left off.

named.name: unseen
named.doc:
The known recipes its tome hasn't shown yet (the new marks):
`known` less those a `Command::Seen` named, bits as `known`.

named.name: reached
named.doc:
The path's milestones it has reached, bits as `known`: bit `i`
is `ContentView.path[i]` (bytes, not a `u64`: a path may have
64 milestones, past what a TypeScript number holds).

named.name: pin
named.doc:
The recipe pinned at the top of its tome: its hand pin
(`Command::Pin`), else the path's (the `pins` of the last
milestone it reached that pins anything), else none.

named.name: pinned
named.doc:
True if `pin` is its hand pin (a `Pin { recipe: None }`
clears it back to the path's).

enum.name: Fight
enum.doc:
What a fight near this connection's body did (FR1): sent to every
connection whose body is within 48 blocks of the husk, as it
happens (a swing's `Hit` just before its `CommandResult`). A Spire
room's fight goes to its run's members only.

enum.name: Gathering
enum.doc:
The shrine's gathering (FR4), to each connection whose body is
within 32 blocks of its ring and to each that joined: when it
opens, as each joins, and as it closes (`open` false).

named.name: closes_ms
named.doc: Milliseconds until it closes and the party goes down.

named.name: joined
named.doc: The players who joined, in join order.

named.name: open
named.doc: False: it closed (the party went down, or nobody joined).

named.name: floor
named.doc: The floor it goes down to (SP2).

named.name: seals
named.doc:
The seals its opener set beside the key (P5.5): spent as it
goes down, if the opener still goes.

enum.name: Run
enum.doc: This connection's player's Spire run (FR4).

enum.name: RootDoor
enum.doc:
Where the shrine's root door is (FR4): the centre of its ring,
where a gathering opens. Sent on connecting, in a world with the
Spire. A client shows the door's ring there and offers to gather
within 12 blocks of it.

enum.name: Spire
enum.doc:
The Spire's news (SP1): the season's week, the sectors freed and
the guardian's first fall. Sent on connecting, in a world with a
Spire on the surface (`Welcome.spire`), and to everyone when any of
it changes (a few times a season). It carried the world-wide key
until P5.F; since P5.1 each floor has its own, forged at an altar
(`Floors.keys`).

named.name: sectors_freed
named.doc: The sectors freed of the Harvest.

named.name: first_kill
named.doc: Who first felled the guardian, if anyone has: the party's names.

enum.name: Floors
enum.doc:
The floors the shrine's root door offers (SP2), with this player's
camps: sent on connecting, in a world with the Spire, again when a
test passed gives it a camp, and when a floor run's close lost it
mana. The door panel draws from it.

named.name: camps
named.doc: This player's camps: bit `n - 1` for floor `n`'s.

named.name: gated
named.doc:
Whether floor `n` needs camp `n - 1` (false until SV1: every
floor is open).

named.name: key_gated
named.doc:
Whether a floor's opener turns its key (P5.1): forged at its
altar, one a run; the root hall is free.

named.name: mana_lost
named.doc:
The mana this player's last floor run lost as it closed (FX.F),
by element (fire, water, wind, earth): what no pool of its own
had room for. Kept by the world until it goes down again, so a
restart still says it. Empty: none lost.

named.name: keys
named.doc:
The keys this player holds for floors 1 to 4 (P5.1): the one
who opens a floor turns one of its key; friends join free.

named.name: seals
named.doc:
The seals a floor's opener may set beside its key (P5.5), with
how many this player holds: forged at the runeforge.

enum.name: Guide
enum.doc:
The field guide (KN4): every species variant found, with who found
it first. Sent on connecting and to everyone when a variant is
first found. The field guide panel draws from it.

named.name: finds
named.doc: The finds, by species then variant.

enum.name: Echo
enum.doc:
An echo rune's ping (SP4, `ToolPower::Echoes`): the block this
connection's player broke at `at` with a charged echo tool, and
the ore within 6 blocks of it, nearest first (at most 24). Sent
only when it found some (a charge spent).

enum.name: SectionUnloadBox
enum.doc:
A box of sections that left the interest area (F4): the client
drops every section it holds from `min` to `max` (inclusive on
each axis), as if each were in a `SectionUnload`. Sent in the chunk
data lane like one, for sections far outside the area: a box never
reaches into the area grown by the unload margin, and nothing the
server still sends lies in it. A whole view left behind (a teleport,
going down into the Spire) is one or a few of these.

enum.name: Helped
enum.doc:
A friend's work reached a milestone of this connection's player's
path (W3T): `by`, whom it trusts, changed something in its land (a
log fed into its campfire, a frame finished there) and the server
judged its path then. Sent to every connection of the player with
the `Knowledge` that reaches it, so the client can say "wren lit
your campfire".

enum.name: Given
enum.doc:
Another player handed this connection's player items (W4S): its
`Drop` at her feet landed in her bag (`Command::Drop`, the bag's
"give to wren"). Live only, never replayed: sent to each of the
receiver's connections as it lands, so the client can say "wren
gave you 9 pebbles".

named.name: count
named.doc: How many came into her bag.

enum.name: Trusted
enum.doc:
Another player began (`on`) or stopped trusting this connection's
player in its land (W4S, `Command::Trust`). Live only, never
replayed (a join sends none for trust given before): sent to each
of the friend's connections as the trust changes, so the client
can say "wren trusts you: you can work their land".

named.name: by
named.doc: The name of the player whose trust changed.

types.name: PlayerId
types.doc: A player's id within one world.

types.name: SpireSite
types.doc:
The Spire on the surface (`Welcome.spire`, SP1): a pure function of the
world's generator and its seed. Clients draw its tower from `foot_y`
to `crown_y` above the column (`x`, `z`), and drain the land's colour
within `blight_r` of it, where nobody builds and wells draw nothing.

struct.name: x
struct.doc: The site's column.

struct.name: foot_y
struct.doc: The top of its foot: where the tower begins.

struct.name: crown_y
struct.doc: Its crown's height.

struct.name: blight_r
struct.doc:
The blight's radius about it, in blocks (`dryad.json` `land.blight`;
0 for none).

struct.name: sectors_freed
struct.doc:
The sectors freed of the Harvest (each a wedge of the blight
healed; 0 until SP5).

types.name: Outcome
types.doc: The outcome of a command.

enum.name: Ok
enum.doc: Applied.

enum.name: Rejected
enum.doc: Refused by the rules or permissions; nothing changed.

types.name: PatchOp
types.doc: One change to an encoded value.

enum.name: Set
enum.doc: Replaces the value at `path` with `value` (encoded).

enum.name: MapPut
enum.doc: Inserts entry `key`, or replaces its value, in the map at `path`.

enum.name: MapRemove
enum.doc: Removes entry `key` from the map at `path`; it must be there.

types.name: PathStep
types.doc: One step of a path into a value.

enum.name: Field
enum.doc: Field `index` (declaration order) of a struct.

enum.name: Variant
enum.doc:
Field `field` of an enum value whose variant is `variant` (both by
declaration order); a tuple variant's value is field 0.

named.name: variant
named.doc: The variant the value must have.

named.name: field
named.doc: The field's index within the variant.

enum.name: Entry
enum.doc: The value of the map entry whose encoded key is `key`.

enum.name: Present
enum.doc: The value inside an option that is present.

types.name: BlockChange
types.doc: One changed block in a `SectionEdit`.

struct.name: index
struct.doc: Its index in the section: `x | z << 4 | y << 8`.

struct.name: block
struct.doc: The block now.

struct.name: facing
struct.doc: Which way it faces.

struct.name: worked
struct.doc: Whether it was placed or cut by a player.

types.name: SectionTimeline
types.doc: One timed block's timeline in a `SectionTimelines`.

struct.name: index
struct.doc: Its index in the section: `x | z << 4 | y << 8`.

struct.name: steps
struct.doc: Its steps, as the `block` query sends them.

types.name: BlockStep
types.doc:
One step of a block timeline: from world time `from` on, the block is
`block` facing `facing` (at growth `stage`, if it grows).

struct.name: from
struct.doc: World time this step starts.

struct.name: block
struct.doc: The block.

struct.name: facing
struct.doc: Which way it faces (north for blocks without orientation).

struct.name: stage
struct.doc: Growth stage, for growing blocks.

types.name: EntityView
types.doc:
A live entity. Live entities exist only in watched areas and are never
persisted; their lasting effects arrive as ordinary block and storage
changes.

struct.name: id
struct.doc: Its id, unique while the server runs, in spawn order.

struct.name: kind
struct.doc: What it is.

struct.name: pos
struct.doc: Where it is: the center of its box's bottom face.

struct.name: vel
struct.doc: Its velocity.

types.name: EntityKind
types.doc: What a live entity is.

enum.name: Item
enum.doc: Some number of one item, flying or lying on the ground.

enum.name: PrimedTnt
enum.doc: Retired (Q4: the TNT left); its tag is never sent again.

enum.name: Player
enum.doc:
Another player's body: a box as wide and tall as the movement
tuning says (0.6 × 1.8). Its id is [`PLAYER_ENTITY_BASE`] plus the
player's id.

enum.name: Creature
enum.doc:
A wild creature, one of a herd: live near a player, or walking its
herd's route farther off (the creature stream). Not world state:
replays and the world's hash never see it. Its id is
[`WILD_ENTITY_BASE`] plus `32 ×` a number the server gives its herd
plus its place in the herd.

named.name: herd
named.doc:
Its herd: the herd's id in the world, its low 53 bits
([`HERD_ID_MASK`], a safe JavaScript integer); the same herd for
as long as the world is.

named.name: member
named.doc: Its place in the herd, the leader 0.

named.name: scale
named.doc: Its size, times the model's (its role's scale times its own).

named.name: variants_set
named.doc:
The model's part switches its role sets (bit `i`: the model's
variant `i`); the rest as the model has them.

named.name: birthplace
named.doc:
Its herd's birthplace variant (KN4): 0 for none, else 1 + an
index into its species' `birthplaces` (its colors).

enum.name: Kept
enum.doc:
A tamed creature: out of her herd, she follows her owner while the
owner is near and present, and rests where she was left otherwise
(world state: the log keeps where). Drawn as the creature she was
(the fields as `Creature`'s); her id is [`WILD_ENTITY_BASE`] plus
`32 ×` a number the server gives her plus her place in her herd.

named.name: following
named.doc: True while she follows her owner.

named.name: home
named.doc:
Her home block, if she is homed (W9): she grazes on her range
about it.

types.name: CreatureRole
types.doc: A wild creature's place in its herd.

enum.name: Leader
enum.doc: The one the rest follow.

enum.name: Adult
enum.doc: A grown member.

enum.name: Young
enum.doc: A young one.

types.name: Velocity
types.doc: A velocity in blocks per step.

struct.name: x
struct.doc: East-west.

struct.name: y
struct.doc: Up-down.

struct.name: z
struct.doc: North-south.

types.name: MovementTuning
types.doc: The content's movement tuning (`movement.json`), every value per tick.

struct.name: gravity
struct.doc: Downward acceleration, blocks per tick².

struct.name: air_drag
struct.doc: Fraction of vertical velocity lost per tick in air.

struct.name: max_speed
struct.doc: Largest speed along any axis, blocks per tick.

struct.name: jump_velocity
struct.doc: Upward velocity of a jump.

struct.name: walk_speed
struct.doc: Walking speed.

struct.name: sprint_speed
struct.doc: Sprinting speed.

struct.name: sneak_speed
struct.doc: Sneaking speed.

struct.name: air_control
struct.doc:
Fraction of the gap to the wished horizontal velocity closed per
tick in the air.

struct.name: swim_speed
struct.doc: Swimming speed.

struct.name: swim_up
struct.doc: Upward acceleration while holding jump in a fluid.

struct.name: climb_speed
struct.doc: Climbing speed.

struct.name: step_height
struct.doc: Tallest obstacle walked onto without jumping, in blocks.

struct.name: width
struct.doc: Player box width, in blocks.

struct.name: height
struct.doc: Player box height, in blocks.

struct.name: glide_fall
struct.doc: Gliding: the fastest fall, blocks per tick.

struct.name: glide_speed
struct.doc: Gliding: the wished horizontal speed.

struct.name: glide_control
struct.doc:
Gliding: the fraction of the gap to the wished horizontal velocity
closed per tick.

struct.name: glide_max
struct.doc: Gliding: the largest horizontal speed on each axis.

struct.name: glide_brake
struct.doc: Gliding: how much a fall faster than `glide_fall` slows a tick.

struct.name: dodge_speed
struct.doc: Dodging: the dash's horizontal speed, blocks per tick.

types.name: MoveMaterial
types.doc: How a block feels to a player's body (`forge_core::movement::Material`).

struct.name: solid
struct.doc: Full-cube collision.

struct.name: climbable
struct.doc: Can be climbed like a ladder.

struct.name: fluid
struct.doc: Present for fluids.

struct.name: friction
struct.doc:
Fraction of the gap to the wished horizontal velocity closed per
tick while standing on it.

types.name: MoveFluid
types.doc: A fluid's movement properties.

struct.name: density
struct.doc: Buoyancy as a fraction of gravity.

struct.name: drag
struct.doc: Fraction of velocity lost per tick.

types.name: MoveState
types.doc: A player body's movement state (`forge_core::movement::MoveState`).

struct.name: pos
struct.doc: Feet position: the center of the box's bottom face.

struct.name: vel
struct.doc: Velocity, blocks per tick.

struct.name: on_ground
struct.doc: Resting on a solid block at the end of the last step.

struct.name: mode
struct.doc: Movement mode at the end of the last step.

struct.name: dodge
struct.doc:
Ticks left of the last dodge (0: ready): dashing for the first
`DODGE_DASH`, i-frames for the first `DODGE_GUARD`, cooling down
after.

types.name: MoveMode
types.doc: How a player's body is moving.

enum.name: Walking
enum.doc: On foot, on the ground or in the air.

enum.name: Swimming
enum.doc: In a fluid.

enum.name: Climbing
enum.doc: On a climbable block.

enum.name: Riding
enum.doc: Riding another entity.

enum.name: Driving
enum.doc: Driving a vehicle.

types.name: ContentView
types.doc: The world's content as clients see it; see `ServerMsg::Content`.

struct.name: packs
struct.doc:
The packs it was loaded from, in load order (each after its
dependencies).

struct.name: names
struct.doc:
The name table: `names[i]` is the name of `NameId(i)`, as in
`Welcome.names` until content changes.

struct.name: blocks
struct.doc: Every block, in id order.

struct.name: items
struct.doc:
Every item, in id order. A block and the item named like it share
an id.

struct.name: recipes
struct.doc: Every recipe, by verb, then input item id.

struct.name: max_stack
struct.doc: The most items one inventory slot holds (and one storage take moves).

struct.name: slots
struct.doc: Inventory slots per player; the first 9 are the hotbar.

struct.name: models
struct.doc:
Every block model (`models/<path>.json`), by name: what a block's
`render.model` names.

struct.name: actors
struct.doc:
Every actor model (`actors/<path>.json`), by name: how players,
creatures, and the dryad look and move.

struct.name: creatures
struct.doc: Every creature species (`creatures/`), by name.

struct.name: hand
struct.doc:
The bare hand (and any item that isn't a tool): percent of a
block's `break_steps` it takes, by the block's `material` (300 is
three times as long); a material not listed takes 100. It breaks
only blocks of tier 0.

struct.name: story
struct.doc:
The opening's story beats (`story.json`), in the order
`ServerMsg::Story.beat` indexes; empty for content without a story.

struct.name: frames
struct.doc:
Every rune frame (`frames.json`), in index order (a `FrameGlow`'s
`frame`): the rune book's pages and the Seer's lens's templates.

struct.name: words
struct.doc: Every rune word (`words.json`), in index order.

struct.name: traits
struct.doc:
Every heritable kin trait (KN4), in bit order: bit `i` of a kept
creature's `traits` is `traits[i]`.

struct.name: path
struct.doc:
The first hour's path (`path.json`, phase 8): its milestones in
order; bit `i` of `ServerMsg::Knowledge.reached` is `path[i]`.
Empty for content without one.

struct.name: voice
struct.doc:
The seed's voice in the tome (`story.json` `voice`, phase 8): by
event, in name order, the line she writes then at each of her
stages. Empty for content without one.

types.name: PackView
types.doc: A content pack's manifest (`pack.json`).

struct.name: namespace
struct.doc: Its namespace (`forge`).

struct.name: version
struct.doc: Its version, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.

struct.name: description
struct.doc: What it adds.

struct.name: dependencies
struct.doc: The namespaces it depends on.

types.name: BlockInfo
types.doc: One block type.

struct.name: id
struct.doc: Its id.

struct.name: label
struct.doc:
Its name for players, if the pack gives one (`"label"`); clients
derive one from the name otherwise ("oak log").

struct.name: description
struct.doc: What it is, for players, if the pack says (`"description"`).

struct.name: solid
struct.doc: Full-cube collision.

struct.name: opaque
struct.doc:
An opaque full cube: a block whose six neighbors are opaque is
hidden (sent as `forge:stone`), and clients skip faces between
opaque blocks.

struct.name: orient
struct.doc: Which facings it accepts when placed.

struct.name: machine
struct.doc:
Its machine's key in `blocks/` (`storage`: a chest, a furnace, a
crucible), if it has one.

struct.name: furnace
struct.doc: A furnace: it burns fuel from its storage and heats what is around it.

struct.name: verb
struct.doc:
A processor's verb (`grind`, `smelt`, `press`): its recipes are the
ones of that verb.

struct.name: drive
struct.doc:
What drives its processor: `heat`, `cold`, or one of the land's
forces, `current`, `wind`, `earth`.

struct.name: interaction
struct.doc: What a right click on it does, if anything.

struct.name: break_steps
struct.doc:
How long breaking it takes at its listed time, in steps (20 a
second; 0 breaks at once). With its `material`, a tool or the bare
hand takes a percentage of it (`ItemInfo::tool`,
`ContentView::hand`): `ceil(break_steps × percent / 100)`. Clients
time a break from that before sending `Break` or `BreakWith`, and
the server refuses breaks well faster than it.

struct.name: unbreakable
struct.doc:
Nothing a player carries can break it (elder wood): a `Break` on it
is refused, so clients say so instead of timing one.

struct.name: replaceable
struct.doc:
A block placed into its cell takes the cell (grass, a flower), the
plant going to the placer as if broken: so a client aiming at it
with a block in hand places into it, not against its face.

struct.name: material
struct.doc:
What it is made of for breaking (`"wood"`, `"stone"`, `"ore"`), if
anything: tools and the hand break each material in their own time.

struct.name: tier
struct.doc:
How hard it is to take: only a tool listing its `material` at this
tier or higher breaks it; 0 breaks by hand (and with anything).

struct.name: render
struct.doc: How it looks.

struct.name: tree
struct.doc:
The part of a natural tree it is, if any: cutting natural wood can
fell a tree (clients time a chop by it and cue a fall).

struct.name: drops
struct.doc:
What breaking it by hand gives, whole items (its `drops`; a leaf's
chance drops aren't here). A client tells from it whether a break
would find room in the inventory.

struct.name: rune
struct.doc:
The part it plays in runework, if any (RW5): a client finds rune
lines, pools and frames by it (their motes, the Seer's lens).

types.name: Orient
types.doc: Which facings a block accepts when placed (its `orient`).

enum.name: None
enum.doc: Any facing is ignored and stored as north.

enum.name: Horizontal
enum.doc: North, south, west, or east.

enum.name: NotUp
enum.doc: Anything but up.

enum.name: Any
enum.doc: All six.

enum.name: Axis
enum.doc:
All six, stored as the positive direction of the axis (up, south,
east).

types.name: Interaction
types.doc: What a right click on a block does besides placing against it.

enum.name: Use
enum.doc:
It is used (`Command::Use`): an elder tree gives its seed, its
keeper eats a dryad tree's ripe fruit.

enum.name: Storage
enum.doc:
It opens: a storage, moved into and out of with `StoragePut` and
`StorageTake`.

enum.name: Runeforge
enum.doc:
It opens a runeforge (RW3): a forge stone, its charge slot and its
rune setting (`Command::Charge`, `Command::SetRune`; the
`runeforge` query).

types.name: RenderView
types.doc: How a block looks (`render` in `blocks/`).

struct.name: shape
struct.doc: How it takes part in meshing.

struct.name: color
struct.doc: sRGB `0xRRGGBB`; null lets the client pick a color from its name.

struct.name: secondary
struct.doc:
Its second color (grass's dirt sides, trims), sRGB `0xRRGGBB`;
null for its color.

struct.name: material
struct.doc: The shader's texture.

struct.name: inset
struct.doc: A cutout's or plant's inset from each face, in 1/32 block.

struct.name: model
struct.doc: The model the client draws for it, by name, if any.

struct.name: form
struct.doc: How a plant stands in its cell (`Cross` for other shapes).

struct.name: emissive
struct.doc: How brightly it glows, 0 to 15.

struct.name: tint
struct.doc: How the climate shifts its color.

struct.name: in_water
struct.doc:
A plant that grows under water: drawn in the water around it, as
if its cell were water, rather than in a pocket of air.

struct.name: parts
struct.doc: What a plant is built from near the eye (`None` for other shapes).

types.name: Shape
types.doc: How a block takes part in meshing.

enum.name: None
enum.doc: Nothing drawn (air).

enum.name: Cube
enum.doc: A full cube: hides its neighbors' faces, blocks sky light.

enum.name: Liquid
enum.doc: A liquid, drawn in the transparent pass.

enum.name: Cutout
enum.doc: A cube inset by `inset`, hiding nothing.

enum.name: Model
enum.doc: Only its model.

enum.name: Leaves
enum.doc: Leaves: alpha-cut, both sides, faces between leaves left out.

enum.name: Plant
enum.doc: A plant: crossed quads (or its `form`), alpha-cut.

types.name: RenderMaterial
types.doc: The terrain shader's procedural textures (`forge_core::RenderMaterial`).

enum.name: Plain
enum.doc: Flat color.

enum.name: Rock
enum.doc: Stone.

enum.name: Grass
enum.doc: Grass top over dirt sides.

enum.name: Sand
enum.doc: Sand.

enum.name: Snow
enum.doc: Snow.

enum.name: Foliage
enum.doc: Leaves, saplings.

enum.name: Planks
enum.doc: Boards.

enum.name: Log
enum.doc: Bark and rings.

enum.name: Dirt
enum.doc: Dirt.

enum.name: Gravel
enum.doc: Gravel.

enum.name: Cobble
enum.doc: Fieldstones in mortar.

enum.name: Clay
enum.doc: Clay.

enum.name: Ore
enum.doc: Stone with flecks.

enum.name: Furnace
enum.doc: Stone bricks with a mouth.

enum.name: Dispenser
enum.doc: Retired (Q4: the dispenser left); its tag is never sent again.

enum.name: Piston
enum.doc: Retired (Q4: the piston left); its tag is never sent again.

enum.name: Sorter
enum.doc: Retired (Q4: the sorter left); its tag is never sent again.
